```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

### Numeric

```{r}
x <- c(0.6, 0.9)
age <- c (20,45,32,11)
summary(age)
```
```{r}
mean(age)
```
### logical
```{r}
x<- c(FALSE, TRUE)
x<- c(T,F)
```

```{r}
#integer
X<- 9:29
#complex
x<-c(1+9i, 4+2i)

#Matrix and operation within matrices
(x<- matrix(1:6, nrow=3, ncol = 3))
(x<- matrix(1:100, nrow=3, ncol = 3))

(y<- matrix(1:6, nrow=3, ncol = 2))
```

### List

```{r}
(x<-list(1,'a', TRUE, 1+4i))

```
### Factor

```{r}
x<- factor(c("yes","yes","no","yes"))
```

### Create a vector with NAs in it

```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, NA, 10, 3) 
is.na(x)
x <- c(1, 2, 4, "NA", 5)  
bad <- is.na(x)  
print(bad) 

x <- c(1, 2, 4, NA, 5)  
bad <- is.na(x)  
print(bad)

x[!bad]

```


What if there are multiple R objects and you want to take the subset with no missing values in any of those objects?

```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, NA, 4, NA, 5) 
y <- c("a", "b", NA, "d", NA, "f")  
good <- complete.cases(x, y)  
good
```
